hadith:
Kafalah - Narrated `Asim:

I heard Anas bin Malik, "Have you ever heard that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, 'There is no alliance in Islam?' " He replied, "The Prophet (ﷺ) made alliance between Quraish and the Ansar in my house."
message: When we recognize Allah as Al-Wahhaab, The Giver of All, and truly believe in His guidance as mentioned in Surah Al-Jinn, we are called to associate nothing with Him in worship and remain grateful for His endless blessings. Just as the Prophet (ﷺ) fostered unity and alliance among believers, we too should strengthen our bonds with one another while keeping our hearts devoted solely to Allah. Let us reflect daily on the provisions we receive and use them to build a community rooted in faith, gratitude, and sincere devotion to our Lord alone.
name:
Al Wahhaab - الْوَهَّابُ - The Giver of All

The origin of Al Wahhaab comes from the Arabic root word 'wahb', which means to give or to donate freely. This name reflects the aspect of Allah's mercy and benevolence, emphasizing that all provisions and resources come from Him. In Islamic tradition, it is a reminder for believers to be grateful for God's endless gifts.
verse:
Al-Jinn - The Jinn - 72:2

It leads to Right Guidance so we believed in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord ˹in worship˺.
